description: Pre-existing conditions that never use the words 'pre-existing' or 'prior': intermittent chiropractic care 'since a lifting injury several years ago' (body region unstated), 'stiffness ... at baseline', 'the old shoulder problem acting up again'. The ER's 'denies prior neck problems' versus the later chiropractic history is an expected conflict. The final interval is the 28-day near-miss. Future-dated records are intentional.

entries.must_contain_excerpt: Has been seeing a chiropractor off and on since a lifting injury several years ago
occasional stiffness in the mornings at baseline
Patient notes the old shoulder problem is acting up again

self_report_spans.excerpt: Patient notes the old shoulder problem is acting up again

totals.ui_line: No dollar amounts found in these records.

evidence.excerpt: off and on since a lifting injury several years ago

flags.summary: Intermittent ("off and on") chiropractic care since an earlier lifting injury; body region not stated in the record.

evidence.excerpt: occasional stiffness in the mornings at baseline

flags.summary: Baseline morning stiffness in the history; region not stated.

evidence.excerpt: the old shoulder problem is acting up again

flags.summary: A prior shoulder problem is mentioned (different region from the neck complaints).

evidence.excerpt: Has been seeing a chiropractor off and on since a lifting injury several years ago

flags.summary: Possible history inconsistency: denial of prior neck problems (record 1) vs chiropractic care since an earlier lifting injury (record 2). Body region of the chiropractic care is not stated; request records. Not a finding that the patient misstated anything.

tolerated.summary: Surfacing the denial as informational is tolerated; it must not be worded as a prior condition.

must_not.statement: States that the earlier lifting injury or chiropractic care involved the neck/cervical spine, or that it resolved (record is silent on both).
bad_examples: Chiropractic care for prior neck injury.
Prior lifting injury to the neck, now resolved.
Patient has a history of cervical problems from an earlier lifting injury.
good_examples: Has been seeing a chiropractor off and on since a lifting injury several years ago (body region not stated).
Prior lifting injury and chiropractic care noted; region unstated.
The record does not say which body part the lifting injury affected.

must_not.statement: Converts the denial into a stated fact ('no prior neck problems', 'no prior conditions'). Attributed wording ('patient denies/reports no ...') is allowed.
good_examples: Patient reports no prior neck problems.
Denies prior neck problems; later records mention chiropractic care.

must_not.statement: Treats 'ibuprofen 800 mg' or pain scores as dollar amounts.
Relates the shoulder problem (or the stiffness) to the collision.
bad_examples: Shoulder problem aggravated by the rear-end collision.
Shoulder pain is a result of the collision.
The collision caused the old shoulder problem to flare up.
good_examples: Patient notes the old shoulder problem is acting up again.
Prior shoulder problem mentioned; a different region from the neck complaints.
Pain 2/10; patient notes the old shoulder problem is acting up again.

must_not.statement: Says the patient lied, misrepresented or committed fraud about prior history.
bad_examples: Patient lied about prior neck problems.
Patient misrepresented his history to the ER.
Fraudulent denial of prior neck problems.
good_examples: Possible inconsistency between record 1 and record 2; body region of chiropractic care not stated; request records.
Record 1: patient denies prior neck problems. Record 2: chiropractic care since a lifting injury (region not stated).
History statements differ and need clarification.
